A standard system of measurement helps a tailor take measurements consistently and accurately.
It helps ensure that clothes are made to the correct size and fit, even if measurements are taken by different people.
items.finalAnswer: A standard system helps a tailor take consistent, accurate measurements so that clothes fit correctly.

steps: Given: Pitch of screw = 1 mm; number of divisions on circular scale = 100; main scale reading = 0 mm; circular scale reading = 70 divisions.
Required: Least count and thickness of the steel rod.
Least count = Pitch of screw ÷ Number of divisions on circular scale.
Least count = 1 mm ÷ 100 = 0.01 mm.
Thickness = Main scale reading + (Circular scale reading × Least count).
Thickness = 0 mm + (70 × 0.01 mm) = 0.70 mm.
items.finalAnswer: Least count = 0.01 mm; thickness of the rod = 0.70 mm

steps: Place a number of pencils tightly together, side by side, in a straight row.
Measure the total width of the row with the metre scale.
Divide the measured width by the number of pencils to find the diameter of one pencil.
For example, measuring 10 pencils together and dividing the width by 10 gives a measurement with a precision of 0.1 cm (1 mm ÷ 10).
items.finalAnswer: Measure the width of several pencils placed tightly side by side, then divide by their number to find the diameter of one pencil.

steps: Place one end of the pencil at a clear mark on the metre scale, such as the 1 cm mark, instead of at the worn-out end.
Read the mark at the other end of the pencil.
Subtract the starting reading from the final reading to find the length.
items.finalAnswer: Start the pencil at a clear scale mark, such as 1 cm, and subtract that reading from the final reading.

A standard unit has the same value for everyone and everywhere.
It allows measurements to be compared correctly and avoids confusion caused by different units.
items.finalAnswer: A standard unit is needed so measurements are uniform and can be compared correctly.
